newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends down on demand slack.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends down on demand slack.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices ended mixed on lack of buying interest and a weak Tokyo futures market, traders said.

At the close, the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board quoted market indicator price for November RSS 1 buyer at 308.50 cents ($1.23) a kg, down one cent from Monday. November SMR 20 buyer was unchanged at 306 cents.
Trading houses quoted the SMR 20 at 304 cents a kg, SMR10 at 305, SMR 5 at 312, SMR L at 343, SMR CV at 361 and drum latex at 234-235 cents.

Traders could not report any sales for the day, saying the market drifted without consumer interest. "It looks like buyers are quite happily stocked at the moment," said a dealer. "The market is going to be flat for a while."
Rains were reducing tapping and supply of raw materials into the market, but prices were likely to be affected only if the bad weather was prolonged until end of the month, said dealers.
The INRO five-day average rose to 238.95 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on Oct 14 from 238.87 on Oct 11. The daily indicator was at 238.82 from 239.35 previously.
